question: A warehouse operates through three shifts. They start with 55 items. In the morning, they divide by 5 for five receiving zones. They multiply by 6 for six distribution routes. They multiply by 5 to scale across five days. They multiply by 7 to project weekly. They add 12 items from corrections. The facility has 11 workers. How many items per week are projected?

A shop operates through the day. They start with 66 items. They multiply by 4 for four daily shifts. They lose 41 items to sales. They add 36 items from restocking. They double the count by 2 for a two-week plan. They add 39 items from delivery. What is their two-week inventory?

A production facility starts with 231 units. They multiply by 8 to scale for eight assembly lines. They multiply by 2 for a double-shift plan. They add 67 units from overflow. They lose 75 units to quality control. Converting to hundreds, what is their final count?

A business starts with 37 dollars. They add 23 dollars from sales. They divide by 3 to split between three partners. They add 65 dollars in new funding. They multiply by 4 to project quarterly returns. What is their quarterly revenue projection?

A warehouse starts with 64 items. They multiply by 8 for eight distribution locations. They lose 406 items to fulfillment. They add 14 items from recovery. They multiply by 5 to forecast five weeks. What is their five-week inventory?

A manufacturer starts with 109 units. They multiply by 3 to scale production. They lose 195 units to orders. They lose 37 units to quality control. They multiply by 9 for a nine-location distribution. They multiply by 4 to forecast quarterly. They lose 745 units to major shipment. The facility has 30 workers. What is their quarterly forecast?

A company starts with 213 dollars. Tom and Sarah compare their budgets. They multiply by 7 to project annual revenue. They lose 407 dollars to expenses. They multiply by 6 for a six-month plan. They divide by 2 to split between two quarters. They divide by 2 again for a monthly breakdown. Converting to cents, what is the monthly budget?

A business operates through the day. They start with 223 dollars in revenue. In the morning, they multiply by 9 for a nine-month projection. By afternoon, they lose 1427 dollars to operating costs. By mid-afternoon, they add 71 dollars from sales. By late afternoon, they lose 634 dollars to vendor payments. By evening, they lose 2 dollars to rounding. Converting to cents, what is their final balance?

A warehouse starts with 150 units. They multiply by 3 to scale for 3 locations. They add 47 units from delivery. They add 32 units from returns. They lose 213 units to orders. The manager has worked 8 years. What is their final inventory?

An artist starts with 87 pieces. He multiplies by 4 to scale for four galleries. He multiplies by 3 for a three-month exhibition. He divides by 2 to split into two collections. He adds 68 pieces from new creations. He multiplies by 4 to forecast four years. He multiplies by 3 for a three-location tour. How many pieces for the tour?

A daycare operates through the day. They start with 100 children in the morning. In the morning, they divide by 5 for five class groups. By mid-day, they add 25 more children. They multiply by 3 for three daily sessions. They multiply by 4 for a four-week program. By evening, they lose 300 children to end-of-day pickups. How many children for the four-week program?

A business manager starts with 117 dollars. Steven and Maria compare their accounts. They lose 112 dollars to operational costs. They add 21 dollars from sales. They lose 8 dollars to fees. They add 37 dollars from interest. Converting to cents, how much do they have?

A factory operates through multiple shifts. They start with 104 units in their morning production. They multiply by 8 for eight manufacturing shifts. They add 56 units from overflow. They add 70 more units from a secondary line. They multiply by 2 to account for two production runs. They multiply by 6 to forecast six weeks. They multiply by 8 to project two months. How many units for two months?

A financial advisor tracks a client's account through the day. They start with 17 dollars. They add 55 dollars from deposits. They add 64 dollars from interest. They divide by 2 to split a portfolio. They lose 48 dollars to a withdrawal. They lose 5 more dollars to fees. They lose 1 dollar to rounding. What is their final account balance?

A store operates through the day. They start with 170 items. Peter and Claire compare their inventory. They lose 97 items to sales. They add 8 items from delivery. They lose 62 items to a return. They lose 15 items to damage. They lose 3 items to miscounting. Converting to dozens, how many items remain?

A business starts with 83 dollars. Jacob and Amanda compare their savings. They double by 2 through matching contributions. They lose 123 dollars to expenses. They add 55 dollars from new income. They add 55 more dollars from interest. Converting to dimes, how many dimes do they have?

A library starts with 66 books. Sarah and Mike compare their collection. They divide by 3 for three reading levels. They add 28 books from donations. They add 19 books from purchases. They add 32 books from more donations. They lose 47 books to wear. What is their final inventory?

An investment account starts with 160 dollars. They multiply by 9 to project annual returns. They divide by 2 to account for taxes. They lose 320 dollars to fees. They lose 395 dollars to market corrections. They multiply by 9 to forecast nine years. What is the nine-year projection?

A student's savings account starts with 96 dollars. They lose 17 dollars to spending. They multiply by 3 for matching program contributions. They add 37 dollars from gifts. They add 52 dollars from part-time work. They lose 14 dollars to a fee. What is their final savings?

A museum operates through the day. They start with 77 artifacts in the morning. They multiply by 9 to forecast nine galleries. They multiply by 8 for an eight-month exhibition. They lose 5450 artifacts to scheduled deaccessioning. They add 17 artifacts from new acquisitions. They add 39 more artifacts from donations. Converting to dozens, what is their exhibition count?

A manufacturer starts with 197 units. They lose 97 units to defects. They double the output by 2 through process improvement. They multiply by 7 to forecast for seven days. They divide by 2 to account for two shifts. They multiply by 5 to project weekly. Converting to dozens, what is the weekly projection?

A business starts with 114 units. They lose 65 units to production. They lose 2 more units to defects. They add 38 units from recovery. They add 11 units from inventory correction. The warehouse has been open 6 years. What is their final inventory?

A warehouse operates through the day. They start with 170 items. In the morning, they add 31 items from delivery. By mid-day, they add 38 more items. By afternoon, they lose 151 items to shipment. They double by 2 for inventory planning. They add 49 items from recovery. Converting to dozens, what is their planned inventory?

A business starts with 183 dollars. Daniel and Sofia compare their accounts. They add 37 dollars from sales. They add 19 dollars from interest. They add 65 dollars from investments. They lose 210 dollars to taxes. They lose 92 dollars to expenses. They lose 1 dollar to rounding. What is their final balance?

A student starts with 107 points. Kevin and Elena compare their scores. They lose 69 points to a failed attempt. They lose 19 more points to a penalty. They lose 14 points to a revision. They lose 1 point to an error. They add 51 points from completing assignments. What is their final score?
